original_excerpt: This qualitative study explores the perceptions, practices, and orientations of 28 Lebanese schoolteachers regarding the integration of AI in school settings. … Reported barriers included insufficient training, lack of institutional support, and concerns related to data privacy and ethical use. … The analysis led to the identification of three qualitative orientations toward AI integration—reluctant users, early adopters, and critical skeptics—reflecting differentiated levels of readiness and engagement.

summary_evidence_spans: This qualitative study explores the perceptions, practices, and orientations of 28 Lebanese schoolteachers regarding the integration of AI in school settings.
Reported barriers included insufficient training, lack of institutional support, and concerns related to data privacy and ethical use.

The analysis led to the identification of three qualitative orientations toward AI integration—reluctant users, early adopters, and critical skeptics—reflecting differentiated levels of readiness and engagement.

claim_text: 來源機構：arXiv；資料標題："Do You Trust It... or Check It?": Exploring Children's Verification Behaviors in Game-Based Human-AI Collaboration；來源刊登日：2026-10-15。作者摘要報告：研究設計一個遊戲式人機協作探測工具，檢視兒童在任務中如何查證 AI 的建議；系統把 AI 建議嵌入生物知識推理遊戲，比較夥伴型、工具型與雙態代理三種互動風格，並以 8 至 10 歲兒童進行初步評估，結合互動紀錄、任務後評分與半結構訪談。（AI 輔助摘要，未經真人逐則審稿；請參閱原文。）

original_excerpt: This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction. … The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent. … A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews.
interpretation_note: 轉述作者摘要的研究目的、系統設計與評估方法；比較三種互動風格屬條件比較，依規則不寫結果。
scope_limitation: 預印本，未經同儕審查（作者註明已獲 HCII 2026 Late Breaking Work 接受）；8–10 歲兒童的初步評估，遊戲情境、非學校課堂；本則不涉及結果。

summary_evidence_spans: This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction.
The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent.
A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews.
